carousel-1-web-form-vs-system.hook: A web form and a referral system look the same on your website. They stop being the same the second someone hits Submit.
carousel-1-web-form-vs-system.linkedin:
A web form and a referral system look the same on your website. They stop being the same the second someone hits Submit.

A web form has one job: collect the details once and send an email. After that, finding it, forwarding it, calling the patient and keeping the referring office posted all depend on someone remembering.

A referral system keeps working. Every referral becomes one case. The X-rays, insurance, messages, status and notes stay on it from the first click to the signed completion note. Your team talks to the referring office right on the case with secure cloud messages, and staff can build notes from templates and copy them straight into your EHR.

That's the difference we care about. It's not just a form. It's a system for your team.

Which one is on your website today?

carousel-2-the-whole-team.hook: Count the people who touch one referral in your office. It's more than you think.
carousel-2-the-whole-team.linkedin:
Count the people who touch one referral in your office. It's more than you think.

The referring office sends it. The front desk finds it and calls the patient. The office manager makes sure nothing slips. The assistant needs the X-rays. The specialist writes the notes and sends the completion note back.

With a web form, each of them is working from a different email, phone message or sticky note. With Tooth Referral, they all work from the same case:

• the referring office sends it complete, and sees the status without calling
• the front desk has every new referral in one list
• the office manager can see who did what, and anyone can pick a case up when someone is out
• the assistant has the X-rays on the case, and can ask for a newer one in a message
• the specialist builds notes from templates, copies them into the EHR, and sends the signed note back

When every team member sees the value, the whole office runs better. That's what a referral system is for.

carousel-3-direct-communication.hook: "Do you have a newer X-ray?" One small question between two offices. Here's how long it takes each way.

"Do you have a newer X-ray?" One small question between two offices. Here's how long it takes each way.

Without a system: a call that nobody picks up, a voicemail, an email to someone's inbox, and a callback the next day while you're with a patient.

With Tooth Referral: Amanda asks right on the referral. Greg at the referring office uploads a current X-ray that afternoon and replies in the same thread.

That's what direct communication looks like. Secure cloud messages between both offices, on the patient's case, HIPAA compliant and encrypted. Inside your own office, administrative notes stay private to your team, and you can @mention a colleague instead of leaving a sticky note.

Less phone tag, more time for patients, and referrals that keep moving.

post-5-web-form-or-system.hook: Web form or referral system? Five questions tell you which one you have.
post-5-web-form-or-system.linkedin:
Web form or referral system? Five questions tell you which one you have:

1. Does each referral become one case, or one more email?
2. Can you message the referring office right on the referral?
3. Can anyone on your team pick it up and see where it stands?
4. Can staff build notes from templates and copy them into your EHR?
5. Does a signed completion note go back when treatment is done?

Mostly no? You have a web form, not a referral system. Tooth Referral is yes to all five, and it takes about five minutes to set up.
